Historically, they were used in low-level programming to identify file formats or memory layouts, and their use has evolved to be more common in higher-level languages. In security systems, magic numbers are used to validate data integrity, such as checking the header of a file to ensure it is not corrupted. Examples include the ASCII value 0x00 for null termination in C, the hexadecimal value 0x494646 in WAV file headers, and the constant 0x55AA used in memory alignment contexts.
